summary: Free T4 is the unbound thyroxine available for your body to use. It is measured alongside TSH because the two together tell you whether a thyroid problem sits in the thyroid itself or in the pituitary gland directing it.
what_it_measures: The concentration of thyroxine not bound to carrier proteins, reported in pmol/L.

interpretations.meaning: A low free T4 with a high TSH is the usual pattern of an underactive thyroid. A low free T4 with a low or normal TSH instead points to the pituitary.
A raised free T4 with a suppressed TSH is the usual pattern of an overactive thyroid.

when_to_seek_help: If you have a fast or irregular heartbeat, marked weight loss, or severe fatigue alongside an abnormal result, contact your GP promptly.
approved_by: Demo dataset (illustrative values, not for clinical use)
